core_obligations: Argue by contradiction: if p contains neither I nor J, choose x in I not in p and y in J not in p (proof lines 2774-2775).
Observe that the product xy lies in IJ and hence in p, contradicting primality, so one of the two ideals is contained in p (proof lines 2775-2777).
proof_roadmap: Pick a witness element in each ideal outside the prime (proof lines 2773-2774).
Multiply the witnesses and read primality backwards from the product (proof lines 2775-2778).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a prime ideal p containing a product IJ of two ideals contains at least one of the factors (statement lines 2767-2771). The proof is a one-step contradiction: witnesses outside p are chosen in each ideal, their product lies in the product and therefore in p, and primality forces one factor to have been in p after all (proof lines 2773-2778). What the short argument uses is that the product IJ lies inside the ideal generated by it, and that primality is available in element-wise form, which is what makes the choice of witnesses worthwhile; the author writes out the whole contradiction. H2.
